newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgian parliament may discuss draft 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Georgian parliament may discuss draft 1997 budget.

text.p: The parliament of the former Soviet republic of Georgia may discuss the government's draft 1997 budget on Tuesday, officials said.
The government set the budget deficit at 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), down from 4.3 percent in 1996.
Annual inflation is seen at 10-12 percent, down from last year's actual inflation of 15 percent and well below the budgeted 1996 price rise of 29 percent.
The rise in GDP is also forecast at 10-12 percent, virtually the same as last year.
Budget revenue is planned at 639.93 million lari, while expenditure will total 839.93 million lari.
According to the draft plan the deficit would be covered by foreign loans and grants from the European Union, the United States and Holland.
